tldr: An external limit on harmful binary response types changes the precision problem for net efficacy in a small randomized trial. The research target is the sharp first improvement below \(1/n\), uniformly over every public integer cap, paired with a total nonlinear rule and matching compatible finite-table priors against all assignment laws. Exact shifted-binomial reduction, asymmetric score information, and rational finite-game brackets support that target. The correction exponents, transition scales, limiting coefficient and boundary conditions are derived outputs. A prospective binary-survival trial supplies the consumer; its cap is specified independently of the observed data.
gap: The unrestricted sharp binary experiment and bounded rectangular minimax game do not state the response-type-budget frontier. A cap destroys the reflection used in the converse and can place a singular score at an observable boundary. The zero-harm endpoint and general spectral principles have older antecedents.
